questions.q: Why is the built-in Account Owner field hidden on our record pages?
o: It costs extra to license
It reads as Stephen on nearly everything, so it is misleading
It was replaced by the Case owner field
It is only visible to administrators
questions.e: It was deliberately hidden during the 1 July 2026 view overhaul so nobody derives ownership from it. Sales Rep is the truth.

questions.q: Claude offers to update the next step on twenty-three opportunities at once. What is the right move?
o: Let it run - that is the point of connecting it
Ask it to list the records and the exact change, then confirm
Refuse and do them all by hand
Run it and check the Sales Pulse tomorrow
questions.e: It has full write access, so a wrong bulk change is a real mess. Read the list first, then let it proceed.

questions.q: Where are comments typed into the daily Pulse emails stored?
o: In the Pulse system only
As a Note on the record, titled with an [Ops Pulse] or [Sales Pulse] prefix
As a Task assigned to Stephen
In the case resolution note
questions.e: Every Pulse comment becomes a CRM Note titled '[Ops Pulse] ...' or '[Sales Pulse] <date> - <record>', attached to the record and its company. The title prefix is how the Pulse reads them back, so it must not be edited.

questions.q: What are our opportunity stages, in order?
o: New, Qualified, Demo, Quote, Closed Won, Closed Lost
New, Screening, Meeting, Proposal, Customer, Closed Lost
Lead, Prospect, Opportunity, Customer
Enquiry, Quote, Order, Delivered, Invoiced
questions.e: New, Screening, Meeting, Proposal, then Customer for a win or Closed Lost for a loss. Customer is our won stage - there is no Closed Won.

questions.q: Someone asks for the value of the pipeline for a board pack. What should you do first?
o: Read the tile and send the number
Check how many open deals carry no amount, and whether the sweep is fresh
Add up the deals by hand
Use the weighted figure instead, since it is smaller
questions.e: Sanity-check before you quote. Deals without an amount are simply absent from the total, and a stale pipeline sweep means the CRM amounts have drifted from the reps' sheets.

o: The total value of all open deals
Amount multiplied by probability, summed across open deals
The value of deals in Commit only
Last quarter's revenue
questions.e: Weighted value is amount multiplied by probability. It is the risk-adjusted view and is always smaller than raw open pipeline - and it excludes any deal with no amount or no probability.

questions.q: Why does that limitation matter for how you work?
o: It does not, you can always forward it
Anything important from an email body must be written into a Note
It means email is not useful
It means you should copy everyone on everything
questions.e: A Note is the only place the substance of an email can live in the CRM. Without it, the record proves a conversation happened but not what was agreed.

questions.q: Where does a comment left through a pulse actually end up?
o: In a spreadsheet the automation keeps
Only in the next pulse email
As a CRM Note titled [Ops Pulse] or [Sales Pulse], attached to the record and its company
As a reply in the sales@ mailbox
questions.e: Comments are stored as CRM Notes with an [Ops Pulse] or [Sales Pulse] title prefix. The prefix is how the pulse reads them back and re-renders them under the item.

questions.scenario: A supplier asks how much business you have in the pipeline for their product this quarter. The dashboard shows an open pipeline value and a weighted value, and you know a lot of deals still have no amount and no close date.
o: Quote the open pipeline tile - it is the official figure
Quote the weighted figure, since it is more conservative
Give the number of live deals and say the values are incomplete, then offer a figure once the amounts are filled
Estimate the missing amounts yourself and add them in
questions.e: Deals with no amount are simply absent from both totals, and a quarter view needs close dates to filter on. The count of live deals is a fact; the value is not yet, and inventing amounts corrupts every roll-up afterwards.
